scripts._comment_gen_android_drugs: Copies the built-in Egyptian formulary from src/lib/drugCatalog.ts into the Android app's DrugCatalog.kt. The website and the phone resolve the same `catalogId` to the same drug, so the two lists cannot be authored separately — edit the TypeScript and re-run this.
scripts._comment_test_rules: Pinned to firebase-tools 13: version 14+ requires JDK 21, and this machine has JDK 11. Install a JDK 21+ and you can drop the @13 to track latest.
scripts._comment_test_permissions: Catalogue hygiene (ids are storage keys), a drift check that every permission the code enforces is one an admin can actually grant, and a check that firestore.rules has not lost a collection from its blanket-write exclusion chain. No emulator needed.
scripts._comment_test_settings: The settings registry against firestore.rules. Every section declares what it writes and who may save; each claim is re-derived from the rules text, so a screen cannot offer a control the database will reject. Written after Prices was gated on access.settings, which the rules accept for nothing that screen writes — the tab opened and every save failed. Also freezes what the rebuild may not break: the ?tab= ids, the tutorial anchors, the assistant's routes, and every settings document name the server routes and the Android app read directly.
scripts._comment_test_phone: Two phone rules that must not be confused: sending refuses a number naming no country, matching accepts every shape one was written in. Conflating them made every patient stored as 01... unreachable on both channels, and made inbound STOP match nobody.
scripts._comment_test_bot: The WhatsApp assistant's decisions, as a pure function. The assertions that matter are the refusals: never answer a clinical message, never talk over a human who has taken the thread, never answer a stop request, and never ask the same question three times.
scripts._comment_test_conflicts: Double-booking detection: a renamed dentist's existing appointments must still block their own slots, and cancellations must release theirs.
scripts._comment_test_ledger: The one place a ledger row is built: every payment carries its dentist, and the lab fee is charged exactly once per procedure.
scripts._comment_test_delete: The one delete rule, shared by every screen: a charge with payments recorded against it cannot be deleted until they are.
scripts._comment_test_allocation: How much of a payment may settle one treatment. A 200 EGP consultation read 'paid 1,400' because four screens disagreed about overpayment and the server, the only one that cannot be bypassed, never asked. Includes the repair cases: an over-allocation already in the books must stay editable downwards.
scripts._comment_test_recyclebin: The recycle bin's boundaries. A server route bypasses firestore.rules entirely, so every limit the rules enforce is re-enforced here or it is gone: path escapes, audit trails, the Admin short-circuit, and a restore that never overwrites.
scripts._comment_test_clinicstatus: Does the server agree with firestore.rules about whether a clinic may still be written to? The rules gate browser writes; the Admin SDK routes bypass rules entirely, so the same decision has to exist in code or an expired clinic keeps taking payments through a route that never asked.
scripts._comment_test_storage: Where uploaded files land. Four of six upload sites had no clinic in the path, two of them flat folders every clinic shares — and a Storage rule cannot scope what the path does not name. Also asserts storage.rules exists and is deployed, since it did not exist at all until 2026-08-24.
scripts._comment_test_storage_rules: The ruleset itself, asked of the rules engine on the storage emulator. storagePaths.test.mjs can only check that a line is present; this uploads, reads, lists and deletes. Written after storage.rules sat undeployed for three days with a Firestore lookup in it that can never resolve in this project.
scripts._comment_test_restore: What a per-clinic restore may touch. The refusals matter more than the copying: users holds clinicRoles for EVERY clinic a person works at, and sms_outbox is drained by a worker that sends without a human and never expires a message. Includes a drift check against the root collections firestore.rules declares, which caught five the hand-written list had missed.
scripts._comment_test_teeth: What the odontogram may claim was done to a tooth. This is a medical record drawn as a picture, so the failure mode is a dentist believing it and being wrong: planned work must never repaint a tooth, an extraction outranks everything done before it, and a treatment colour must never be mistakable for a diagnosis colour.
scripts._comment_test_clinicscope: Every money and clinical write must name its clinic. The routes otherwise fall back to the caller's defaultClinicId, so a procedure logged at a second clinic was priced, attributed and written into the first one — visible only as 'Choose the dentist' for a dentist who was on screen. The API client attaches it now; this stops that becoming a per-call-site duty again.
scripts._comment_test_misplaced: Telling a record in the wrong clinic's books apart from a patient deleted since, and from a row nothing can judge. The last one matters most: two write paths left no evidence either way, and a report that counts them as clean overstates what it knows.
scripts._comment_test_repair: The historical payment repair's classifier. The assertions that matter most are the ones that refuse to touch a row whose commission was corrected by hand.
scripts._comment_test_discount: Price lists and discounts. The two rules that matter: the lab fee is never discounted, and commission is calculated on the net.
scripts._comment_test_branches: Price lists scoped to branches: one default per scope, and no branch quoting another branch's rates.
scripts._comment_test_briefing: The arithmetic behind the daily and weekly brief: double-counted revenue, lateness read on the clinic clock, absence claimed before a shift starts. No network, no emulator.
scripts._comment_test_modeltext: Markdown/bidi/injection cases for the model-text renderer used by the printed treatment plan. No network, no emulator.
scripts._comment_test_theme: Preset completeness, mint-matches-globals.css, token guards, and the boot script executed against a fake DOM. The boot script is a string the compiler never sees.
scripts._comment_test_tokens: The AI token meter: one credit spans several API rounds, and the counts must survive a response that carries no usage block. No network, no emulator.
scripts._comment_test_ainav: The allowlist behind the assistant's navigate_to tool. Guards the failure where it announces 'Opening the patient's file' and pushes a 404. No network, no emulator.
scripts._comment_test_aiwrite: Who may ask the assistant to change a record. The route runs on the Admin SDK, so firestore.rules never sees these writes and this table is the only thing standing in for them: a receptionist must not get clinical.edit by going through the chat instead of the screen.
scripts._comment_test_lab: Lab case tracking: the per-branch code, searching by the number written on a bag, the twelve work types and which fields each one prints, and the order sheet in all three paper sizes. The one assertion worth reading is that a patient's full name never reaches the paper.
scripts._comment_test_leadwelcome: The instant reply to a new ad lead, and above all which field name the clinic's WhatsApp token is stored under. The fixtures used a name nothing writes, so the suite passed while every real clinic silently fell back to the manual queue with auto selected and credentials saved.
scripts._comment_test_leadinterest: Reading the service out of a Facebook campaign name. The Arabic assertions are the point: the definite article glues onto the noun, so substring matching invents matches, and a keyword that skips the normaliser can never fire at all. Both directions are pinned because loosening one is how the other regresses.
